_meta.what: the meter's own per-model credit rates, fitted from the passive stretches already in the repository. `measured_rates` is the block tracker/credits.py reads; everything else is the working the fits show.
_meta.no_traffic: read-only arithmetic over committed files; no account was driven

measured_rates.unit: credits per input token; the output rate is output_multiplier times it

dave/post.qualification: the anchor is exempt from the dominance rule

jwork/post.qualification: the anchor is exempt from the dominance rule

jwork/pre.qualification: the anchor is exempt from the dominance rule

opus.why: the unit anchor: 0.6667 credits per input token (5x that per output token), which is what a credit means in this repository. The fit rescales its Opus coefficient to this figure, so every rate beside it is measured relative to it and none of them tests it. If this row is wrong every credit figure scales with it and nothing in our stretches would show it.

dave/post.qualification: 9 of its 32 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Sonnet; pooling needs 3

jwork/post.qualification: 1 of its 26 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Sonnet; pooling needs 3

jwork/pre.qualification: 1 of its 51 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Sonnet; pooling needs 3

sonnet.why: pooled from dave/post only. A fit contributes to a family's rate only if at least 3 of its stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on it, and jwork/post (1 of 26), jwork/pre (1 of 51) fall short, so their coefficients for Sonnet are extrapolated from a minority column and stay on the record in per_fit without entering the rate.

haiku.status: not measurable, no fit has 3 clean stretches that are 60% or more Haiku

jwork/post.qualification: 0 of its 26 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Haiku; pooling needs 3

jwork/pre.qualification: 0 of its 51 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Haiku; pooling needs 3

haiku.why: the highest Haiku share of any clean stretch on a fitted account is 0.257. 2 fits return a coefficient for it, but a fit contributes to a family's rate only if at least 3 of its stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on that family, and none does (jwork/post 0 of 26, jwork/pre 0 of 51). A coefficient fitted from a minority column is whatever the majority columns leave, so neither a value nor an interval is published. The per-fit coefficients are on this record. The reference figure stands beside this row, untested by our data and used in no arithmetic.

dave/post.qualification: 0 of its 32 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Fable; pooling needs 3

jwork/post.qualification: 3 of its 26 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Fable; pooling needs 3

jwork/pre.qualification: 2 of its 51 stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on Fable; pooling needs 3

fable.why: pooled from jwork/post only. A fit contributes to a family's rate only if at least 3 of its stretches carry 60% or more of their raw tokens on it, and dave/post (0 of 32), jwork/pre (2 of 51) fall short, so their coefficients for Fable are extrapolated from a minority column and stay on the record in per_fit without entering the rate.

opus-5-5.status: not measurable, no clean stretch is Opus 5.5-heavy
opus-5-5.why: the highest Opus 5.5 share of any clean stretch on a fitted account is 0.000, and no fit includes Opus 5.5 at all, so there is nothing to measure a rate from. There is no reference figure for Opus 5.5 either: the January table predates it.

measured_rates.method: delta_pct = sum over families of (input + cache_write + 5x output) x rate, plus a cache-read column, by non-negative least squares over every clean stretch of the account and side of 2026-09-14, with the Opus coefficient rescaled afterwards to 0.6667 credits per token so the fit reads in credits. Intervals are 80% bootstrap intervals over resampled stretches. A family's rate is the median of the per-fit point estimates and its interval is the union of theirs, whether or not the fits agree (`agree` records that, and `why` says what the disagreement is). Only fits with at least 3 stretches carrying 60% or more of their raw tokens on the family are pooled (the anchor is exempt); the others stay in per_fit with `qualified: false`, and a family no fit qualifies for is withheld with a status sentence. A family whose pooled interval reaches zero is withheld too, value and interval both: the fit cannot separate it from free.
